questions.q: Where does the Snowflake connector live in Power BI Desktop's Get Data dialog?
options: It's a separate standalone app, not part of Get Data
Under the Database category, alongside Redshift and BigQuery
Under a dedicated Cloud Warehouses category
Under the Files category
questions.explain: Snowflake sits alphabetically among other database connectors, not in a separate cloud-specific bucket.

questions.q: What are the two required fields in the Snowflake connection dialog, and why is one a cost decision?
options: Username and Password — the only two fields needed
Role and Database — selected before authenticating
Database and Schema — selected before anything else
Server and Warehouse — whatever warehouse is entered is the compute footprint that burns credits on every query this report runs
questions.explain: Server and Warehouse are required up front; the warehouse choice directly determines ongoing compute cost for this report.

questions.q: Which two models should be selected in Navigator for this chapter's work?
options: `int_orders__joined` and `raw_orders`
Every model in the project, to be safe
`fct_orders` and `customers` — the marts layer only
`stg_jaffle_shop__orders` and `stg_jaffle_shop__payments`
questions.explain: Finance and Ops only need the business-facing marts layer — staging and intermediate models stay internal to the dbt project.

questions.q: Which load option fits this capstone's fct_orders, and why?
options: Import — fct_orders is already incrementally maintained in Snowflake, so a scheduled refresh after dbt run is enough
Live connection only, with no refresh schedule needed
DirectQuery, because the data changes every second
Neither — Power BI can't connect to an incremental dbt model
questions.explain: Since fct_orders is already kept current by dbt's incremental build, Import with a scheduled refresh is the right fit, not live DirectQuery.

questions.q: Why shouldn't Power BI connect directly to `int_orders__joined` or a staging model?
options: There's no real reason — it would work fine either way
Power BI technically cannot connect to any model other than fct_orders
Staging and intermediate models are deleted after each dbt run
It would expose implementation details not meant to be business-facing — exactly why the marts layer exists
questions.explain: The whole point of a marts layer, planned back in Lesson 2, is to be the business-facing surface — Finance and Ops never need to know int_orders__joined exists.
